# Density — quality-first context compression for DSH

A DSH client plugin that compresses **only the tool output it can compress without losing
answers**,
archives the originals, and keeps a per-context-window ledger of what it saved.

It is deliberately conservative: the goal is information density (remove noise), not a
smaller token
bill. Token savings are a side effect.

*The sidebar panel, rendered from sample data: pressure against the native trigger line,
savings, th
e per-window ledger, and anchor stability.*
## What it does — and what it refuses to do
| Input | Action | Why |
| JSON / JSONL arrays | convert to CSV (every value kept) | lossless in practice; 5/5 in blind tests

|
| Unified diffs | drop unchanged context lines | changed lines and hunk headers stay |
| Logs | k
eep head, tail, every error line, plus a `[统计]` aggregate line | counts stay answerable after sampli

ng |
| Tables | **never compressed** | row sampling destroyed 5 of 6 answers in testing |
| Prose /

long text | **never compressed** | sampling a narrative is data loss, not a summary |
| Source code
| **never compressed** (v30+) | reviewers always recalled the outline; the round trip cost more than

it saved |
| `cairn_*`, `density_recall` output | **never touched** | memory is the only copy in co

ed |
| `cairn_*`, `density_recall` output | **never touched** | memory is the only copy in context |

When a tool result *is* compressed, the replacement carries a marker such as
`[density #density-1a2b

3c4d · 原文 4210B · 用 density_recall(marker) 取回]`, and the full
original is archived under `~/.density

/archive/<session>/`. The model can pull it back with
the lazily-registered `density_recall` tool (o

nly registered after the first compression, so
idle sessions pay no schema cost).

## Configuration
| Key | Default | Meaning |

| `mode` | `shadow` | `shadow` measures only; `safe` / `balanced` enable the entry path |
| `write`

| `false` | rewrite tool results (the actual compression switch) |
| `policy` | `quality` | `quality
` = this document's table; `strict` = diffs only; `aggressive` = legacy sampling (tables, head/tail,

code outline) |
| `surface` | `false` | extract per-turn cards and replace finished turns (off by d

efault; changes the prefix) |
| `protectedTools` | `['cairn_']` | tool-name prefixes that are never

compressed |
| `archiveDir` | `~/.density/archive` | where originals are stored |
| `ledgerDir` | `~
/.density/windows` | per-window ledger |
## What you can observe

- **Panel**: sidebar entry 「密度」, Chinese UI, cards for capacity, pressure, savings,
anchors, mirror,

native compaction and the window ledger.
- **`GET /density/snapshot`**: JSON with the live window a

nd the last 8 windows.
- **Ledger**: `~/.density/windows/<sessionId>.jsonl`, one JSON line per windo

w snapshot.
A window is an epoch (same provider, model, context size and trigger line). Survives res

tarts.
- **Metrics**: `~/.density/shadow/<sessionId>.jsonl` — every compression, recall and turn car

rts.
- **Metrics**: `~/.density/shadow/<sessionId>.jsonl` — every compression, recall and turn card.

ools/replay.mjs` — replay persisted DSH session logs through the entry compressor.

ession-id.mjs` — repair sessions written by older versions without message ids.

## Publishing notes

The working copy is installed as a **profile link** (`link:D:/.../density-panel`) under the
name `@l

ocal/density-panel` with `"private": true`, which keeps accidental npm publishes
impossible. To publ
ish under your own name:

1. rename the package in `package.json` (e.g. `dsh-density-panel`), drop `"private"`;
2. copy the na

me into `cordis.patch.yml` (`name:`) so the bundle id matches;
3. reinstall the bundle in your DSH p

ch.yml` (`name:`) so the bundle id matches;
3. reinstall the bundle in your DSH profile and restart.
## Known limitations
- Compression is extractive; it cannot summarize semantics. That is why prose and code are skipped.

- Log sampling loses non-error lines; the `[统计]` line only restores aggregate counts.
- Recall costs

about the size of the original — cheap only when recalls are rare.
- The UI is Chinese-only today.
